key_insight: Co2In improves continual learning by separating fast adaptation from durable storage through a bi-level memory system that encodes, consolidates, and integrates knowledge.
engineering_relevance: For data-driven constitutive modeling, this offers a practical way to update models with new loading regimes while reducing catastrophic forgetting of earlier material behavior.
method: Working memory learns new data and encodes knowledge into parameters.
A consolidation step extracts patterns from parameters and compresses them into a compact knowledge representation.
The knowledge representation is integrated into long-term memory as separate network layers for stable retention.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet under exemplar-free Class-IL and Task-IL settings, where it achieved state-of-the-art performance with efficient memory use.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the consolidation and integration steps preserve prior knowledge without overfitting to new tasks, especially in more complex real-world datasets.
paper_title: Co2In: a Bi-level Memory Incremental Learning Framework with Knowledge Encoding, Consolidation, and Integration
